subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: John Dawson <john.dawson@finsecure.com>

Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up on data isolation

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the team's time. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we work through ops/security requirements for our upcoming pilot:

- Data residency/isolation: our product processes regulated PII and payment data. We need assurance that inference requests and any derived embeddings/outputs do NOT leave our control plane or are persisted to Redwood-managed storage in a way that would violate our policy.
- Control plane: is a private control plane (customer-managed) available for the Private VPC option? If not, what are the guarantees around network segmentation and access?
- Logging & audit: what logs are retained (request/response payloads, inference metadata, model versions) and for how long? Is audit logging configurable to ship to our SIEM?
- KV cache & caching behavior: does Redwood persist prefix/KV cache to any shared storage? If so, can that be restricted to our VPC?
- KMS/BYOK: does the Private VPC support customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption at rest?

Can you confirm which deployment mode best fits the above (Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem), and share any SOC2/network diagram/SLA materials we can share with procurement/security? Also looking for a rough timeline and ballpark cost differential so we can align with stakeholders.

Thanks,
John Dawson
Sr. Product Security
FinSecure

> - KV cache & caching behavior: does Redwood persist prefix/KV cache to any shared storage? If so, can that be restricted to our VPC?

Thanks for the clear list, John — below is a concise recap and next steps. Mateo and I can jump on a 30-min technical call to walk through details and network requirements; Marissa will scope commercial/timeline.

Quick answers / summary:
- Dedicated capacity: provides isolated GPU pools (dedicated instances) in Redwood-managed infrastructure. Customer inference payloads are processed on dedicated instances and are isolated at the instance level; however, the control plane (orchestration, model placements, scheduling) and some management metadata remain in Redwood's managed control plane/network. For many customers this meets compliance with tight contractual controls + BYOK, but it does not provide a customer-owned VPC.
- Private VPC (VPC-hosted or on-prem): provides customer-managed networking and the option for a private control plane. In this mode we can deploy the control plane components into your VPC or on-prem environment (subject to network review) so that sensitive traffic never traverses Redwood-managed networks. This is the recommended path if your requirement is that request payloads and orchestration metadata must stay within your network boundary.
- Logs & retention: by default we retain operational logs and minimal inference metadata for X days for observability. For Private VPC we can configure audit log forwarding to your SIEM (Syslog/S3/Kinesis) and set retention policies per contract. Request/response payload persistence is opt-in only and can be disabled.
- KV cache: the runtime uses in-memory and ephemeral GPU-local KV caching; we do not persist KV cache to shared Redwood storage unless explicit long-lived caching is configured. For Private VPC we can restrict any cache persistence to your storage endpoints.
- KMS/BYOK: supported for Private VPC and for Dedicated (with attached customer KMS). We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS bring-your-own-key) and HSM options for Private deployments.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_design.pdf (network/control-plane diagram + checklist), SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level controls overview).

Next steps:
1) Mateo — can you join a 30-min tech call next Tue/Wed (Feb 24/25) to walk networking/KMS details?
2) Marissa will provide a ballpark cost and expected onboarding timeline for both options.
3) We'll share the Private VPC playbook + network checklist (attached) and SOC2 summary.

If it helps, for initial pilot customers that require strict isolation we recommend starting with Private VPC to avoid later migration work.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — adding a few commercial and timeline notes so FinSecure can plan with procurement: 

- Ballpark pricing: Dedicated capacity typically has a lower TTM and lower initial engineering overhead; for your pilot size (approx 8-12 RPS peak) the monthly committed spend estimate is in the range $XXk-$YYk depending on model family and quantization. Private VPC incurs a one-time onboarding/integration fee (network review, KMS integration, control plane deployment) plus a slightly higher recurring cost to cover private control plane resources.
- Timeline: Dedicated onboarding can be completed in ~2-3 weeks once SOW and PO are in place. Private VPC onboarding is ~6-8 weeks (network changes, KMS/HSM integration, security review) depending on availability of network/infra resources on your side.
- Procurement docs: we can provide a draft M.A.P and SOW; SOC2 summary attached for initial review. Full SOC2 report can be shared under an NDA if needed.

Happy to set expectation calls with procurement/legal. If you want to lock calendar for a tech deep-dive, Rachel’s suggested slots next week look good for us.

Cheers,
